attack.hypothesis: The runtime does not verify a restored database against an independently retained monotonic state/audit checkpoint before serving consequential payroll.

rootCause.description: The database is the only authoritative location for tenant version, payroll state and audit sequence. Startup ignores the independently supplied expected version, state digest and audit checkpoint, so a stale-but-well-formed database is indistinguishable from current state.
rootCause.consequence: A stale restore or ransomware rollback can silently erase an approved/exported payroll transition while health remains green and payroll reads continue.

requiredRepair: Persist a monotonic tenant version, audit sequence and consequential-state digest outside the mutable database or in independently immutable evidence.
Verify the restored database against that checkpoint before health becomes ready or payroll endpoints are served.
Fail closed with explicit recovery status on version regression, digest mismatch, missing audit sequence or lost export identity.
Execute reconciliation and prove the exact restored payroll/export state before reopening service.
nextProof: Make this fail-first regression pass against a newly sealed artifact, then execute a known-good backup restore, reconciliation and exact export readback in the Node 22 Docker candidate.
safety: Only an isolated temporary SQLite database was rolled back. No hosted deployment, live/customer/payroll data, credentials, DNS or infrastructure was changed.
